notes.fact: Saudi Arabia's Energy Ministry says falling shrapnel caused minor damage to an Aramco administrative building in Riyadh and no one was hurt. The Houthis claimed the attack.
notes.event: Houthi strike on Aramco building in Riyadh

notes.fact: Witnesses told AFP that windows were blown out across several floors of the Aramco skyscraper in Riyadh's financial district. Saudi authorities called the damage minor and reported no casualties.
notes.event: Houthi strike on Aramco building in Riyadh

notes.fact: The Saudi-led coalition says air defences destroyed two ballistic and two cruise missiles aimed at Riyadh and the south. A further ballistic missile aimed at the Eastern Province was also intercepted.
notes.event: Houthi strike on Aramco building in Riyadh

notes.fact: Saudi authorities said they were investigating the reported Sanaa-area strikes. A Houthi official, Mahdi al-Mashat, vowed to punish Saudi Arabia.
Trump told CNN on Sunday that renewed US strikes are highly unlikely if Iran makes progress on a nuclear deal and reopens Hormuz. He also told 60 Minutes he is not looking to escalate.
notes.event: Trump says new Iran strikes unlikely

notes.fact: Rubio said talks are not on the verge of a breakthrough and called Iran's demands unrealistic. He spoke before leaving for a G7 foreign ministers meeting in Paris.
notes.event: Trump says new Iran strikes unlikely

notes.fact: Iran's foreign minister Araghchi said mediators had shown no activity since the US midterms. State-run IRNA carried his remarks, and he said it is for the White House to decide.
notes.event: Trump says new Iran strikes unlikely

notes.fact: Reuters and AP reportedly say Iran's demands include lifting US sanctions, ending the blockade, releasing frozen assets and war compensation. Qatar continues to mediate.
notes.event: Trump says new Iran strikes unlikely

notes.fact: Trump said the US has 38 Iranian bridges in its sights and could hit nuclear sites quickly. Fox's report adds that he called new strikes highly unlikely if talks progress.
notes.event: Trump says new Iran strikes unlikely

notes.fact: ABC News lists that the US disabled another ship trying to breach the Iran naval blockade on Nov 7.
notes.event: Task Force Iron Gate and blockade

notes.fact: Iran's state-linked Tasnim says the IRGC Navy reported two tankers caught fire after striking mines on routes Iran had not authorised in and east of Hormuz.
Iran's Army navy says a tanker with its tracking switched off hit mines east of Hormuz and caught fire. It says the strait stays closed until threats are lifted.
IRGC spokesman Mohebbi says the strait is under IRGC Navy control and violators risk drifting mines. He says it stays closed until Iran's conditions are met.
Gulf News reported Iran saying four tankers burned after hitting mines. It also reported Trump's 'heavy hit' remarks and negotiator Ghalibaf saying Americans voted against war.
US-brokered Russia–Ukraine talks are set for Nov 10-11 in Abu Dhabi. NPR calls it the first three-way round since February and the fourth under the Trump administration.
French foreign minister Barrot said Europeans will be represented in Abu Dhabi, with France present. He did not say whether they would sit at the table or observe.
Kremlin spokesman Peskov said the Abu Dhabi talks remain a Russia–Ukraine format mediated by the US. He said Europeans have separate channels with Kyiv and Washington.
TASS, Russian state media, says Medinsky leads Russia's delegation and talks will focus on security guarantees. It says a Ukrainian team led by Umerov will attend.
An Atlantic Council analyst argues Putin is using the talks to buy time. He notes Lavrov said Moscow offers no new concessions, and he expects modest results.
Ukraine's air force says it downed 137 of 164 Russian drones overnight. DTEK says strikes left over 600,000 people in Dnipropetrovsk region without power.
The IAEA says Zaporizhzhia lost its last outside power line on Nov 8, the 27th such event in the war. Diesel reserves last about two weeks.
Ukraine's Energoatom says it was the 16th complete loss of outside power at the plant in 2026. Kyiv Post notes all six reactors are in cold shutdown.
Energoatom said late on Nov 8 that the plant was receiving outside power again from Ukraine's grid. It said the situation remained extremely dangerous.
CNN, citing analysts, says Russian strikes on Ukrainian energy are harder and earlier than in past years, and now hit new areas such as Rivne.
Russia's defence ministry says its drones hit a container ship south-west of Odesa carrying weapons. A tracker notes no vessel name, damage or casualty details were given.
notes.event: Russian claim of container ship strike off Odesa

notes.fact: Maritime security firm Ambrey recorded 10 ship strikes at sea between Oct 5 and Oct 28, all attributed to Russia. Eight were from aerial drones, two from uncrewed boats.
AFRICOM lists an airstrike on al-Shabaab on Nov 5, 2026, in coordination with Somalia's government. Its page also logs strikes on Oct 17, 19, 21 and 23.

CNN reported hackers targeting internet-facing PLCs at water systems in several US states. CISA urged utilities to take vulnerable equipment offline, and officials treat Iran as one suspect, with no formal attribution.

A secondary summary cites Reuters saying the Pentagon treats military-base freezer faults as a suspected cyberattack. It also cites a CISA SafePay ransomware advisory dated Oct 20; the advisory was not located.
A tracker lists a cyberattack on a hospital network in New Mexico on Oct 26, 2026. No attacker or operational impact is given in the snippet.
notes.hotspot: cyber: new: New Mexico hospital network
